8:["$","$L13",null,{"data":{"chapterId":17,"verseId":13,"chapterTitle":"Examination of Action and Fruit","totalVerses":33,"verseData":{"id":"v17_13","number":13,"title":"The Buddha's Own Analysis: Introducing the Correct View","sanskrit":{"text":"","transliteration":"","translation":"I will then explain what is tenable here: The analysis propounded by all Buddhas, self-conquerors And disciples according to which . . ."},"philosophy":{"insight":"Nāgārjuna introduces his own analysis, claiming it aligns with ALL enlightened beings — Buddhas, Pratyekabuddhas, and Śrāvakas. This isn't HIS innovation; it's the authentic teaching of all awakened ones. The claim is bold: the Mādhyamika view is the true intent of ALL Buddhist schools.","madhyamaka":"Nāgārjuna presents the yukti (tenable analysis) propounded by sarva-buddha (all Buddhas), pratyekabuddha (self-conquerors), and śrāvaka (disciples). This establishes his analysis as the authentic Buddhist teaching, not an innovation. The Mādhyamika view claims to be the true meaning (nītārtha) of the Buddha's words.","quantum":"The Copenhagen interpretation claimed to be the correct, consistent framework for QM after classical failures. Like Nāgārjuna: \"The previous framework failed; here is the correct one, endorsed by the founders.\" Every paradigm shift claims to be the right interpretation.","bridge":"Both Nāgārjuna and paradigm-shifting physicists claim their framework is the correct interpretation of the founders' work. Nāgārjuna: \"This is what all Buddhas taught.\" Copenhagen QM: \"This is what the equations mean.\" Both: the new framework claims continuity with the tradition while revolutionizing it.","accessible":"Nāgārjuna says: \"Now I'll explain the correct view — the one that ALL awakened beings have taught.\" He's not inventing something new; he's recovering the authentic teaching that the opponents misunderstood. Like a physicist saying: \"Let me show you what the equations REALLY mean.\"","twoTruths":"The \"tenable analysis\" will operate at the ultimate level (emptiness) while preserving the conventional level (karma functioning). The two truths framework is the foundation of the correct view — both truths working together, not one replacing the other.","commonMisconception":"NOT saying Mādhyamika is a new invention by Nāgārjuna. He claims it's the authentic interpretation of what ALL Buddhas taught. Whether this claim is historically accurate is debated, but it's Nāgārjuna's explicit position."},"quantumResonance":{"concept":"Paradigm-Consistent Reinterpretation","score":48,"strength":"Low","explanation":"New frameworks often claim continuity with tradition — QM claims to extend (not replace) classical physics in its domain. Nāgārjuna claims his view extends (not replaces) the Buddha's teaching.","caveat":"This is a sociological/rhetorical parallel about how paradigm shifts are presented, not a physical parallel."},"animation":{"visualBridge":"Three figures (Buddha, Pratyekabuddha, Śrāvaka) converging their light beams into a single teaching — the correct analysis of karma. Nāgārjuna receives and transmits this unified teaching.","educationalGoal":"User sees Nāgārjuna presenting his analysis as the authentic Buddhist teaching, endorsed by all enlightened beings."},"deeperDive":[{"q":"Who are the \"self-conquerors\"?","a":"Pratyekabuddhas — enlightened beings who attain liberation independently, without a teacher in their final life. They realize dependent arising through personal contemplation but don't teach extensively. Including them shows the teaching's universality across ALL types of awakening.","realLifeExample":"Self-taught scientists who discover the same laws as institutionally trained ones. The truth is the same regardless of how you arrive at it. Pratyekabuddhas = independent discoverers; Buddhas = full teachers; Śrāvakas = students."},{"q":"Why claim all three endorse this view?","a":"To establish UNIVERSALITY: the teaching isn't specific to one school, teacher, or vehicle. ALL awakened beings, regardless of their path to awakening, teach the same fundamental analysis. This is a strong claim for the Mādhyamika view.","realLifeExample":"Multiple independent labs verifying the same experimental result. If everyone who looks carefully arrives at the same conclusion, the conclusion is likely correct. Universal endorsement = universal truth."},{"q":"Is this claim historically accurate?","a":"Debated. Nāgārjuna's claim is that the Buddha's teaching of dependent arising, when properly understood, implies emptiness (as in the Heart Sutra). Other schools (Sarvāstivāda, Sautrāntika) disagree, claiming the Buddha taught inherent existence of dharmas. This is the central debate of Buddhist philosophy.","realLifeExample":"Different interpretations of the US Constitution: each side claims the founders' endorsement. Nāgārjuna claims the Buddha meant emptiness; other schools claim the Buddha meant dharma-existence. The debate continues."},{"q":"What will the \"tenable analysis\" contain?","a":"VV.14-21: karma as empty, nonexpiring, functioning through dependent arising. Key concepts: (1) Karma as debt/promissory note (v.14). (2) Karma requiring meditative wisdom, not mere abandonment (v.15). (3) Emptiness = nonannihilation (v.20). (4) Non-arising = nonexpiring (v.21).","realLifeExample":"A professor's lecture outline: \"Now I'll explain the correct theory. It has these components: A, B, C, D.\" V.13 is the introduction; vv.14-21 are the components."},{"q":"How does this verse function rhetorically?","a":"It claims authority (all Buddhas endorse this), creates anticipation (what IS the correct analysis?), and establishes continuity (not innovation but recovery of authentic teaching). It's a powerful rhetorical setup before the content begins.","realLifeExample":"A TED talk opening: \"What I'm about to share isn't my idea — it's what the greatest minds have always known. Here's why we forgot it, and here's how to recover it.\" Authority + anticipation + continuity."},{"q":"Does the ellipsis (\"...\") at the end matter?","a":"Yes — the verse is deliberately incomplete. It sets up vv.14-21, which complete the thought. V.13 is a grammatical bridge: \"The analysis according to which...\" → vv.14-21 specify WHAT that analysis says. The incompleteness creates forward momentum.","deeper":"V.13 is one of the rare verses where Nāgārjuna explicitly claims his view aligns with the Buddha's own teaching. Throughout the MMK, he typically argues through logic (prasaṅga) rather than authority (āgama). V.13 is an exception: he invokes all three types of enlightened beings to endorse his analysis. This is strategically important because it preempts the objection: \"You're inventing a new teaching.\" Response: \"No — I'm recovering what all Buddhas taught.\""}],"quiz":{"beginner":{"question":"Whose analysis does Nāgārjuna claim to present?","options":["A) His own invention","B) The analysis of ALL Buddhas, Pratyekabuddhas, and Śrāvakas — the authentic teaching of all enlightened beings, not a new invention.","C) Only his teacher's","D) An unnamed philosopher"],"correct":"B","explanation":"Nāgārjuna claims his analysis is endorsed by ALL types of enlightened beings — universally valid, not personally invented."},"intermediate":{"question":"Why does v.13 claim universality across all three types of awakened beings?","options":["A) Name-dropping","B) To establish that the teaching isn't school-specific but universal — anyone who awakens, regardless of path, arrives at the same analysis.
